newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's OTOB wants to become Eastern Europe centre.
newsitem.headline: Austria's OTOB wants to become Eastern Europe centre.

text.p: Austria's Futures and Options Exchange (OTOB) on Monday said its new family of eastern European stock indices should help it become a centre for investors interested in that region.
"We want to become a knowhow centre for eastern Europe," Guenter Schiendl, the exchange's product development manager, told a news conference.

OTOB last month introduced a product family of four national indices of actively traded blue chips as well as the CECE Index, a regional capitalisation-weighted benchmark composed of 41 members of the four national indices.
The four indices are those of the Czech Republic, Hungary, Popland and Slovakia.
"The indices were composed for the typical British or German broker or dealer as well as for international funds specialising in eastern Europe," Schiendl said.
He added local indices were often tailored to domestic investors only and barely useable as an underlying instrument for derivatives.
"This is an international line of products for an international market, denominated in an international currency, the U.S. dollar," Schiendl said.
Stock exchange officials in the region have voiced concern that OTOB's new product range would compete with other options and derivatives being developed locally.
